page: Vultr vcg-a16-48c-496g-128vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 48 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs, 24 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, and 496.0 GB of system memory. The hardware profile is distinguished by its integration of eight NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, delivering a combined 128 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 1500 GB NVMe SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 73907.77 and a PassMark CPU score of 55603.55. Single-core performance is average, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1781.09. Memory performance is mixed; small-block cached read bandwidth is strong at 4709.75 GB/sec, and large-block write bandwidth is strong at 101.16 GB/sec, whereas large-block read bandwidth is average at 124.75 GB/sec. In database operations, the server demonstrates strong throughput with 74.78 million Redis SET operations per second.

The eight NVIDIA A16 GPUs enable high-throughput parallel processing. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier performance for prompt processing, reaching 8182.48 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 610.38 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are strong for the 7B model at 32.71 tokens/sec and average for the 135M model at 248.63 tokens/sec. This hardware density makes the server highly cost-efficient for multi-tenant GPU workloads, VDI hosting, and medium-scale LLM inference, though the 2.0 GHz CPU clock speed presents a tradeoff for single-threaded CPU-bound tasks.
